source.title: Sparsification and Reconstruction from the Perspective of Representation Geometry
source.authors: Wen-Jie Sun; Bing-Zhe Wu; Zhi-Le Yang; Chengke Wu

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments on SAE representation geometry, but does not measure feature superposition, capacity competition, neuron polysemanticity, SAE recovery accuracy or completeness, or the dimensionality of individual superposed features as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition as motivation and studies how pretrained SAEs change representation geometry. Its own Case 1 rank-variability findings and Case 2 local/global geometry findings concern SAE representations, but do not directly test any listed version. Case 3 intervenes on local-representation separability and reports reconstruction error; it does not measure a claim version. The paper also reports cluster counts, MSTW, and Procrustes disparity in Case 2; these characterize representation geometry rather than a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained SAEs on GPT2-Small, Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B as a tool and reports its own geometric analyses: rank variability under noise, local and global cluster geometry, and reconstruction MSE under latent interventions. None of its measures shows superposition, capacity competition, polysemanticity causes, SAE feature recovery or completeness, or the dimensionality of individual features. Superposition appears only as motivation, so T4 fits better than the record's T6. The paper uses the SAE dictionary premise but does not test it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors claim three things: SAE latent representations are stratified, sparse encoding reduces feature overlap by merging similar features and adding dimensions, and increasing separability between local representations causally lowers reconstruction MSE. The conclusion's sentence saying separability decreases reconstruction performance contradicts Table 2, Table 8 and the abstract. It appears to be a wording error.
record.recipe_differences: The cited original is a toy-model study of superposition; this paper analyzes pretrained SAEs on language-model residual streams using noise perturbations, clustering, dimensionality/topology metrics, and optimization interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary across model-concept pairs; the authors state that 7 out of 9 pairs increase in Avg. ID and 7 out of 9 increase in Betti 0.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 9 model-concept pairs, sparse encoding raised local-cluster Avg. ID in 7 and Betti 0 in 7, and lowered global MSTW in 8. Pythia-70M Weekdays and Chemical Elements decreased in Betti 0, and Pythia Chemical Elements decreased in Avg. ID. The authors read these changes as reduced feature overlap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse encoding by pretrained SAEs reshapes local and global representation geometry, with direction varying by model and concept.

record.problems: The paper says prompt selection does not guarantee capture of all concept representations and does not control SAE regularization. The conclusion section says increased separability leads to a decrease in reconstruction performance, contradicting the body, tables, and abstract, which report improved reconstruction performance. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the Case 2 comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No rows from Case 1 or Case 3 were included: Case 1 reports rank and geodesic-distance changes under noise, and Case 3 reports reconstruction error under interventions, but neither measures a listed claim version. Case 2 cluster counts, MSTW, and Procrustes results were also left out because they do not measure a listed version; the aggregate findings are summarized in fits_no_version.

untested.parts: No toy models, no feature-count versus dimension sweep, no sparsity transition, no geometry of feature directions.
No test of capacity competition or of important features getting dedicated dimensions.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemantic neurons.
Pretrained SAEs are taken as given. Their recovery of sparse features and the spread of features across neurons are not measured.
Case 1 rank changes under noise concern latent-tensor stratification, not whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units.
Avg. ID of about 2.6–4.2 is computed for HDBSCAN clusters of UMAP-reduced token activations, not for individual superposed features. There is no 1-D versus multi-D feature comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The 'feature overlap reduced' interpretation rests on geometric proxies (Avg. ID, Betti 0) of UMAP+HDBSCAN clusters, without controls, uncertainty estimates or comparison to a non-SAE baseline. Appendix B.3 cites Liu et al. on superposition scaling with model size but does not measure it. The Table 1 row values match the text.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, sparse feature-over-dimension sweep, interference measurement, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular-geometry test.
No test of neuron polysemanticity as capacity competition or of important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether it evidences superposition.
The paper analyzes pretrained SAE latent representations in language models, but does not establish that features are spread across neurons or validate SAE feature recovery.
No test of SAE features as complete, stable, or canonical units.
The reported intrinsic dimensionality is for local representations or clusters, not individual features in superposition; no comparison of one-dimensional and multidimensional features.
